primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy leading to end-stage renal disease (CKD stage 5)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (CKD assessment and management) and NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria

medications.dose: As per sliding scale / patient’s regimen
medications.duration: Lifelong – review at each clinic visit
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management essential for CKD patients (NG203)

medications.duration: Discontinue – replace with loop diuretic (see furosemide)
medications.purpose: Current antihypertensive (ineffective at eGFR 4 mL/min/1.73 m²)
medications.nice_justification: Thiazides lose efficacy when eGFR <30; NG203 recommends loop diuretic instead

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily, titrate up to 80 mg twice daily as needed
medications.duration: Lifelong – review BP and electrolytes every 1‑3 months
medications.purpose: Volume control and hypertension in CKD stage 5
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends loop diuretic when eGFR <30 for BP and fluid management

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 statin for all CKD patients

medications.dose: Weight‑based, e.g., 0.45 µg/kg subcutaneously once weekly
medications.duration: Until haemoglobin 100‑120 g/L, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treatment of anaemia of CKD (Hb <100 g/L)
medications.nice_justification: NG107 ESA for anaemia of CKD when iron stores adequate

medications.medication: Ferric carboxymaltose 1000 mg IV single dose
medications.dose: 1000 mg administered intravenously over 15 min (single dose)
medications.duration: Single dose; repeat if ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20 % after 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Repletion of iron stores prior to ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NG107 iron supplementation for CKD iron deficiency

medications.medication: Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg PO three times daily with meals
medications.dose: 800 mg three times daily with meals, titrate to target phosphate <1.5 mmol/L
medications.nice_justification: NG107 phosphate binder for CKD stage 5 with phosphate >1.5 mmol/L

medications.dose: 0.25 µg once daily, adjust according to calcium/PTH
medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor calcium, phosphate, PTH every 3‑6 months
medications.purpose: Management of secondary hyperparathyroidism / vitamin D deficiency
medications.nice_justification: NG107 vitamin D analogue for CKD‑MBD

medications.medication: Sodium bicarbonate 500 mg PO three times daily
medications.dose: 500 mg three times daily, titrate to maintain serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L
medications.nice_justification: NG107 sodium bicarbonate for CKD metabolic acidosis

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer can bind atorvastatin and reduce its absorption
interactions_checked.action: Take atorvastatin at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after sevelamer

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause hypotension and electrolyte shifts
interactions_checked.action: Start furosemide at low dose, monitor BP and electrolytes within 1‑2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: ESA may raise blood pressure; concurrent ACE‑I may mask rise
interactions_checked.action: Check BP after each ESA dose and adjust antihypertensive therapy as needed

interactions_checked.interaction: IV iron can cause transient hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Observe patient for 30 min post‑infusion; manage hypotension if occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased sodium load may blunt antihypertensive effect
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and adjust lisinopril dose if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 4.1 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the minimum 20 mL/min required (NICE TA775)
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis (NICE contraindication)
CKD stage 5; NSAIDs accelerate renal decline (NG203 contraindicated)
Patient already on ACE‑I; adding an ARB would increase hyperkalaemia and AKI risk (NG203)

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium, phosphate, calcium, PTH, bicarbonate, ferritin, TSAT, Hb, lipid profile, and blood pressure values are not available – baseline labs must be obtained before initiating ESA, iron, phosphate binder, vitamin D analogue, sodium bicarbonate, and statin dose titration.
Patient weight not recorded – ESA dose calculated using an estimated 70 kg; adjust after weight is known.
Allergy history not provided – verify no hypersensitivity to statins, sevelamer, iron preparations, or vitamin D analogues before prescribing.
Adherence may be limited by psychosocial barriers; arrange community nursing support and medication reminders.
treatment_summary: The patient with CKD stage 5 secondary to diabetic nephropathy should continue ACE‑I (lisinopril) and insulin, replace thiazide with a loop diuretic (furosemide) for better BP/volume control, start high‑intensity atorvastatin for CV risk reduction, and address CKD‑MBD and anaemia with sevelamer, alfacalcidol, sodium bicarbonate, darbepoetin alfa and IV iron once iron deficiency is confirmed. Contraindicated agents (SGLT2‑i, metformin, chronic NSAIDs, ARB) are avoided. Baseline labs and regular monitoring per NG203/NG107 are required.
